question: How can measurement error and missing values be handled inside a Bayesian model instead of being averaged away or dropped?
hypothesis: Stating assumptions about error and missingness as part of the generative model lets conditional probability propagate them, giving more honest estimates than ad hoc fixes.
contributions: Measurement error on outcome and predictor via parameters for true values with Normal(obs, SE) likelihood
MCAR Bayesian imputation of neocortex in the primate milk data
Improved imputation model using predictor association

limits: Missingness treated only as MCAR; MNAR is described in a paragraph with no worked model (14.2.3).
Imputation model assumes Gaussian N although it is a proportion bounded in 0-1 (left to practice problems).
Age at marriage is treated as exact; the author notes the information in it may be illusory.
WAIC is switched off for measurement-error models because default code does not integrate over div_est.
Uses map2stan/rethinking and Stan syntax of the 1st edition (<- assignment in Stan), dated by the 2nd edition's ulam.
No sensitivity analysis of the Gaussian-error assumption beyond 'try different assumptions'.
practices: Replace an observed datum with a distribution whose mean is a parameter when its standard error is known (14.1.1, p.426).
Use a Gaussian for the error when only the SD is known; it is the maximum entropy choice, not a claim that error is Gaussian (p.426).
Put error on predictors the same way, one parameter per unknown true value (14.1.2, p.429).
Do not average data before analysis; model the distribution instead (p.431).
Do not drop incomplete cases; model the variable with missing values jointly with the outcome (14.2.1, p.432).
Make the imputation model use associations among predictors (14.2.2, p.435).
Model the joint distribution of all variables, and vary assumptions to test sensitivity (p.436-437).
Raise adapt_delta to 0.95 to remove divergent iterations in error models (p.428).
Turn off default WAIC when the likelihood has latent estimates (p.428).

terms.definition: Missing Completely At Random: the location of the missing values is completely random with respect to those values and all other values in the data.
